title: Railway breach leads to $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges
content_md: Cloud hosting provider Railway says hackers exploited vulnerabilities in its infrastructure to steal customer authentication secrets and generate approximately $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage, potentially exposing credentials for up to 100,000 workspaces. The company disclosed the incident on October 22, warning customers to rotate their secrets after detecting unauthorized access to systems storing environment variables. In a new incident report published today, Railway confirms that attackers gained access to its internal source code and the decrypted customer environment variables for at most 1.85% of its workspaces, or approximately 100,000. The company says this figure represents the maximum number of potentially impacted workspaces, rather than the confirmed number whose secrets were stolen. The attack began on October 20, when hackers exploited a previously unknown vulnerability in Railway's build infrastructure to escape filesystem isolation and obtain an internal credential. The attackers used the credential to access stored build histories and retrieve a copy of Railway's internal source code, which they then analyzed to identify additional ways to compromise the platform. The attackers then exploited a second vulnerability involving an improperly configured trust relationship to gain further access to Railway's infrastructure and obtain credentials used to decrypt customer environment variables.
